title: Slippery Slope Misalignment treats any misalignment as serious because incremental drift compounds into systemic failure
content:
A.0.1.1.12 names Slippery Slope Misalignment as "the shortest path to misalignment," where incremental misaligned acts are justified by one of four moves: ignoring significance because the scale is small; the triviality of how the misalignment occurred; the good intentions of the actor; or the conviction that the ends justify the means.

Enumerating the *justifications* rather than the acts is what makes this operational — the pattern is recognizable at the moment of rationalization, before consequences appear.

The stated consequence is deliberately absolute: "any misalignment at all is always very serious and, if not dealt with, results in increased risk of disequilibrium and alignment failure," which for Sky means governance attack or financial collapse. This is why the Atlas contains Immutable Documents — a zero-tolerance stance needs a component that cannot be incrementally amended, or the doctrine erodes by the very mechanism it warns about.
description: Small scale, triviality, good intentions and ends-justify-means are named as the four justifications that enable drift; unchecked, the endpoint is governance attack or financial collapse.
